mission: The ANU Catholic Society is the home of Catholic students on campus. As a society with strong Dominican origins, our motto - Fides et Ratio, Faith and Reason - draws from St Thomas Aquinas, who taught that rigorous intellectual inquiry and a life of deep faith are not opposing paths but complementary pursuits that lead to truth.
In this spirit, the Society provides a nourishing Catholic community that supports ANU students as they grow in faith and deepen their understanding of the world at university.

We organise a wide range of events: weekly Mass, volunteering initiatives, social gatherings and academic lectures. These provide opportunities for spiritual, intellectual and personal growth, while strengthening the bonds of friendship among our members.

patron: Our patron is Pope St John XXIII, whose name is also carried by the Catholic residential college beside our chapel. His commitment to education and social justice is a legacy the Dominican Order has continued at ANU.

Our motto, Fides et Ratio - Faith and Reason - expresses the conviction at the heart of the Society: that the search for truth in the lecture theatre and the search for God in the chapel are the same search, seen from two sides.
history: Catholic life at ANU has deep roots. The Dominican friars established a presence beside the university, and John XXIII College - founded under Dominican auspices - has been a home for Catholic students since the 1960s. The St John the Evangelist Chapel on Daley Road remains the centre of Catholic worship on campus.

The Society today continues that tradition: Mass and the sacraments each week, formation in the intellectual tradition of St Thomas Aquinas, service with Caritas and Vinnies, and an open door for every student who walks past.
historyGaps: We are piecing together the Society's own institutional history - including its founding date and its story after 1975. John XXIII College has recently published its history, which records some of the origins of Catholic student life at ANU.
If you were part of CathSoc in decades past, we would love to hear from you: anucathsoc@gmail.com.
